title: Tool saga conductor: progressive aborts, result scoping, and loop dampening
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Complex user requests can trigger multi-tool sagas where tools call other tools or the model in loops. We need a conductor that orchestrates multi-tool chains while: 1) preventing unbounded recursion/looping, 2) ensuring tool result injection is scoped and sanitized, 3) preserving streaming delivery to the client when possible, and 4) remaining compatible with older SDK call shapes.

Goal: Implement a "Tool Saga Conductor" runtime component that supervises the execution graph for a single user request, applies progressive abort rules, scopes and sanitizes tool outputs before injection into the model context, and exposes a compatibility shim so older SDKs and integrations see the same semantics.

Design highlights:
- Saga sessions: each multi-tool execution gets a saga session id. The conductor tracks depth, wall-clock time, token consumption, and tool-call fanout per session.
- Progressive abort policy: thresholds (depth, tool fanout, token usage, time) trigger a graded response: soft-throttle -> partial abort (halt further tool calls but continue model decoding) -> hard-abort with structured error. Thresholds are tunable per-customer tier and route.
- Result scoping: tool results are tagged with provenance and scoped to sub-contexts. Injection rules control whether a tool's output becomes part of the prompt prefix, appended to the assistant message, or stored in ephemeral KV (not auto-injected). This prevents accidental prompt bloat and leakage across parallel sagas.
- Sanitization and type-checking: before injection, outputs pass structured-output validators and schema transformers. Malformed results are replaced by a normalized failure object to avoid prompting the model with unstructured garbage.
- Streaming compatibility: when streaming to clients, the conductor allows streaming of model tokens while tool calls resolve in the background. If a tool abort is escalated, the stream emits a structured stop token and a final status payload.
- Backwards compatibility shim: older SDKs that assume synchronous tool-call semantics get a compatibility flag that makes the conductor block the top-level response until critical tools complete (with a configurable timeout), preserving expected behavior for legacy integrations.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict scoping reduces unintended contamination of prompts but increases the complexity of prompt construction and could slightly raise latency for small chains.
- Aggressive progressive abort thresholds protect platform capacity but risk truncating legitimate long-running orchestrations; we'll expose per-route tuning to balance this.
- Blocking for compatibility increases tail latency; default behavior favors streaming-first, with blocking only enabled when the route or customer opts in.

Non-goals: full distributed saga persistence (we rely on ephemeral session state for now), changing public SDK APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor assigns a saga session id to multi-tool chains and records depth/fanout metrics
Progressive abort states implemented (soft-throttle, partial-abort, hard-abort) and configurable per-route
Tool outputs are tagged with provenance and can be scoped to injection modes (prefix, assistant-append, ephemeral-kv)
Structured-output validators run before injection and malformed outputs are normalized
Streaming continues during background tool calls; stream emits structured stop and final status on escalation
Compatibility shim available to block top-level response until selected tools finish with a configurable timeout
Telemetry emitted for every saga session (duration, tokens, depth, abort-reason) and visible in Console rollout debug view
Automated unit+integration tests cover recursion scenarios, fanout storms, and graceful abort under load
